review.title: New States and federal territory
review.plain: Congress may admit new States, but no State may be formed within another State or by joining States without the consent of the State Legislatures and Congress. Congress may make all needful Rules for the Territory and other Property of the United States.
powers: New States may be admitted by the Congress into this Union
shall have Power to dispose of and make all needful Rules and Regulations respecting the Territory or other Property belonging to the United States
limits: no new State shall be formed or erected within the Jurisdiction of any other State

provisions.what: New States may be admitted by the Congress into this Union

no new State shall be formed or erected within the Jurisdiction of any other State; nor any State be formed by the Junction of two or more States, or Parts of States, without the Consent of the Legislatures of the States concerned as well as of the Congress

forming a State by the Junction of two or more States, or Parts of States
exceptions: with the Consent of the Legislatures of the States concerned as well as of the Congress

review.title: Republican government and protection of States
review.plain: The United States shall guarantee every State a Republican Form of Government and protect each against Invasion, and, on Application of the State Legislature or Executive, against domestic Violence.

provisions.what: The United States shall guarantee to every State in this Union a Republican Form of Government
The United States shall protect each of them against Invasion
The United States shall protect each of them against domestic Violence
conditions: on Application of the Legislature, or of the Executive (when the Legislature cannot be convened)

review.title: Amending the Constitution
review.plain: Congress proposes Amendments when two thirds of both Houses deem it necessary, or calls a Convention on the Application of two thirds of the State Legislatures. Amendments become valid when ratified by three fourths of the States. No State, without its Consent, shall be deprived of its equal Suffrage in the Senate.

shall call a Convention for proposing Amendments
limits: no State, without its Consent, shall be deprived of its equal Suffrage in the Senate

provisions.holder: The Legislatures of two thirds of the several States
conditions: on the Application of the Legislatures of two thirds of the several States

provisions.what: Amendments, in either Case, shall be valid to all Intents and Purposes, as Part of this Constitution, when ratified by the Legislatures of three fourths of the several States, or by Conventions in three fourths thereof, as the one or the other Mode of Ratification may be proposed by the Congress
requires: ratified by the Legislatures of three fourths of the several States, or by Conventions in three fourths thereof
conditions: as the one or the other Mode of Ratification may be proposed by the Congress

review.title: Debts, supreme Law of the Land and oaths
review.plain: Debts from before the Constitution remain valid against the United States. The Constitution, federal Laws and Treaties are the supreme Law of the Land, binding State Judges. Federal and State officers must swear to support the Constitution, but no religious Test may be required for office.
powers: shall be the supreme Law of the Land
limits: no religious Test shall ever be required as a Qualification to any Office or public Trust under the United States

provisions.what: All Debts contracted and Engagements entered into, before the Adoption of this Constitution, shall be as valid against the United States under this Constitution, as under the Confederation

This Constitution, and the Laws of the United States which shall be made in Pursuance thereof; and all Treaties made, or which shall be made, under the Authority of the United States, shall be the supreme Law of the Land
conditions: Laws of the United States which shall be made in Pursuance thereof
Treaties made, or which shall be made, under the Authority of the United States

provisions.what: the Judges in every State shall be bound thereby, any Thing in the Constitution or Laws of any State to the Contrary notwithstanding

The Senators and Representatives, and the Members of the several State Legislatures, and all executive and judicial Officers, both of the United States and of the several States, shall be bound by Oath or Affirmation, to support this Constitution
provisions.binds: Senators, Representatives, Members of the State Legislatures, and all executive and judicial Officers of the United States and of the several States

review.title: Ratification of the Constitution
review.plain: Ratification by the Conventions of nine States is sufficient to establish the Constitution between the States so ratifying it.

provisions.what: The Ratification of the Conventions of nine States, shall be sufficient for the Establishment of this Constitution between the States so ratifying the Same
requires: The Ratification of the Conventions of nine States

review.title: Freedom of religion, speech, press, assembly and petition
review.plain: Congress shall make no law respecting an establishment of religion or prohibiting its free exercise, or abridging the freedom of speech or of the press, or the right of the people peaceably to assemble and to petition the Government for a redress of grievances.

the right of the people peaceably to assemble, and to petition the Government for a redress of grievances

review.title: Right to keep and bear arms
review.plain: Because a well regulated Militia is necessary to the security of a free State, the right of the people to keep and bear Arms shall not be infringed.

limits: shall not be infringed

review.title: No quartering of soldiers
review.plain: No Soldier shall in time of peace be quartered in any house without the Owner's consent, nor in time of war except in a manner to be prescribed by law.

review.title: Searches, seizures and warrants
review.plain: The right of the people to be secure in their persons, houses, papers, and effects against unreasonable searches and seizures shall not be violated. No Warrants shall issue but upon probable cause, supported by Oath or affirmation, particularly describing the place to be searched and the persons or things to be seized.

review.title: Grand jury, double jeopardy, self-incrimination, due process
review.plain: No person shall be held to answer for a capital or infamous crime without a Grand Jury indictment (with military exceptions), twice put in jeopardy, compelled to witness against himself, or deprived of life, liberty, or property without due process of law; nor private property taken without just compensation.
limits: No person shall be held to answer for a capital, or otherwise infamous crime, unless on a presentment or indictment of a Grand Jury
nor shall any person be subject for the same offence to be twice put in jeopardy of life or limb
nor shall be compelled in any criminal case to be a witness against himself
nor be deprived of life, liberty, or property, without

review.title: Rights of the accused at trial
review.plain: In all criminal prosecutions, the accused has the right to a speedy and public trial by an impartial jury of the State and district of the crime, to be informed of the accusation, to confront witnesses, to compulsory process for witnesses, and to the Assistance of Counsel.

to be informed of the nature and cause of the accusation
to be confronted with the witnesses against him
to have compulsory process for obtaining witnesses in his favor
to have the Assistance of Counsel for his defense

review.title: Jury trial in civil cases
review.plain: In Suits at common law where the value in controversy exceeds twenty dollars, the right of trial by jury shall be preserved, and no fact tried by a jury shall be re-examined in any Court of the United States except according to the rules of the common law.

review.title: Electing the President and Vice-President
review.plain: Electors vote by distinct ballots for President and Vice-President and send sealed lists to the President of the Senate, who opens them before both Houses. A majority of Electors appointed is needed; otherwise the House chooses the President, voting by states, and the Senate chooses the Vice-President.

the Senate shall choose the Vice-President
limits: no person constitutionally ineligible to the office of President shall be eligible to that of Vice-President of the United States

provisions.what: The Electors shall meet in their respective states, and vote by ballot for President and Vice-President, one of whom, at least, shall not be an inhabitant of the same state with themselves; they shall name in their ballots the person voted for as President, and in distinct ballots the person voted for as Vice-President

The President of the Senate shall, in the presence of the Senate and House of Representatives, open all the certificates and the votes shall then be counted
The person having the greatest number of votes for President, shall be the President, if such number be a majority of the whole number of Electors appointed
